authorshipDisclosure: Did not author the album merge repair or its three new regressions. Previously authored portions of the underlying soundtrack model/storage/bundle and bonus-offload framework. This follow-up independently reviews the new repair, not all historical album functionality.
scope: Preservation of filename-bearing v3 album metadata and declared genre/role/energy/theme tags during additive album merge into v1/v2/v3 libraries; unchanged conflict, rights, original-byte, shared-budget and concurrent-writer boundaries.
fingerprintAlgorithm: fieldKitRecipeSources(readFile): SHA-256 of the raw bytes of the eleven audio inputs concatenated in their listed order.

reviewedRepairs.problem: A filename-bearing v3 album could be appended to a v1/v2 object before upgrading its format, causing the original-filename schema guard to reject the addition.
reviewedRepairs.resolution: The helper first upgrades the existing owned library whenever either side is modern. It preserves existing tracks, playlists, assignments and selection; explicit v2 listening choices remain intact with recordingMode:false added by the established upgrade helper.
reviewedRepairs.regression: A first filename-bearing v3 album upgrades an empty v1 library; a populated-v1/v2 case preserves assignments, selection, original metadata and explicit v2 listening settings.

reviewedRepairs.problem: The helper replaced incoming source tags with generic legacy genre inference, so an acoustic/menu/energy 2/Ukrainian-theme recording could become synth90s/any/energy 3/retro.
reviewedRepairs.resolution: New track IDs receive their verified incoming tags when present. Existing track IDs retain the listener's tags. Legacy inference remains only for incoming records without declared tags.
reviewedRepairs.regression: Declared tags survive addition and remain eligible for the acoustic menu queue; a repeated import preserves listener overrides and exact original bytes.

boundaryChecks: isPreparedSoundtrackLibrary and exact canonical equality between the verified incoming library and the selected album declaration remain mandatory before merge.
Same-ID tracks and playlists still require identical canonical metadata; conflicting identities refuse rather than overwriting edits. The incoming tag exception applies only to newly added IDs.
No declaration, URL path, permission, catalogue admission or fetch behavior was relaxed. Tags carry selection metadata only; they confer no network or rights authority.

Album merge returns an owned draft. Actual persistence remains explicit through the established prepare/commit path, CAS generation and shared media budget; no read path or helper directly writes a store.
Exact wanted hash/byte completeness, no-extra-assets checks, SHA-based deduplication and the 256 MiB combined managed limit are unchanged.

Bonus offload/restoration still retains reference identities and editor changes, preserves bytes shared with other uploads, requires explicit verified downloads, and protects atomic generations on refusal.
Frozen v2 readers/writers remain unchanged and reject v3 rows without modifying audio, media or story domains. Expanded genres still require v3.

The compiler source was read only for the integration contract: it emits v3 libraries with original fileName and per-track tags, making the repaired path necessary. This report does not approve its rights register, musical classification or publication decisions.
The previous ten reviewed audio inputs are byte-identical. soundtrack-albums.mjs is now the eleventh source in the functional-audio recipe; the new fingerprint includes that repair.
result: No unresolved P1/P2 defect identified in the bounded final-source album repair. Functional source approval only for the stated eleven-input fingerprint and delta; prior source-review limitations remain applicable.
boundaries: No runtime source, tests, ledger, generator, production record, or expected presentation pin was edited by this reviewer in this follow-up.

The three pre-fix regressions were supplied by the repair author; this reviewer independently inspected their failure mechanisms and ran the final complete 28-test cohort, not a reconstructed pre-fix runtime.

Synthetic fixture decoding and modeled storage/transport tests do not prove native audibility. No new browser, full repository, frozen build, offline install, physical-device, or full production-history gate was run by this reviewer here.

No original or licensed composition, recording, artist identity, cultural accuracy, musical quality, genre assignment, artwork, license/rights evidence, gameplay-video status or public release is approved.
